authors.bio: Yassine builds and maintains iKnowAPDF, including the in-browser PDF engine behind its compression, merging, signing and editing tools. These guides explain what he has learned building and testing those tools.

articles.title: How to Sanitize PDF Metadata and Hidden Layers Before Court or Public Release
articles.seoTitle: Sanitize PDF Metadata Before Court Filings
articles.description: Where hidden author names, XMP metadata, old revisions and form data live inside a PDF, and how to strip them in your browser before you publish or file.

toolCta.title: Strip PDF Metadata & Rebuild the File Locally
toolCta.description: Clear the /Info fields, remove the document-level XMP stream, drop old incremental revisions and optionally flatten forms — processed in your browser.

blocks.text: When publishing legal briefs, FOIA disclosures, investigative reports, or corporate filings, visual inspection is never enough. Sensitive data regularly leaks from PDFs because someone drew a black rectangle over confidential text, or because the file still carries hidden metadata and earlier drafts. In this guide we look at where hidden data lives inside the PDF format (ISO 32000) and how to clean a document in your browser before it leaves your hands.
The Fatal Mistake: Visual Black Boxes vs. Removing the Underlying Data

Many people assume that placing a black rectangle over sensitive text makes it unreadable. However, a PDF page is built from separate layers and object dictionaries. When you draw a shape over text with a basic markup tool, the underlying characters remain intact in the page's /Contents stream. Anyone who opens the file can press Ctrl+A, copy the text, or run a command-line extraction utility to read everything underneath. Our guide to [true PDF redaction](/blog/permanent-pdf-redaction-vector-graphics) covers how to actually remove that text.
Inspecting Raw PDF Metadata Dictionaries

Even when the visible text is clean, PDFs produced by Microsoft Word, macOS, Adobe InDesign, or office scanners usually embed a Document Information Dictionary (/Info) and often an XMP metadata packet (/Metadata). Inspect a typical file with a hex editor or `pdfinfo` and you will often find usernames and file names like these:

blocks.title: Example /Info Dictionary
blocks.code:
12 0 obj
<<
  /Title (Settlement_Agreement_FINAL_v4_Redline.docx)
  /Author (j.miller@lawfirm-internal.local)
  /Creator (Microsoft® Word for Microsoft 365)
  /Producer (macOS Version 15.2 (Build 24C101) Quartz PDFContext)
  /CreationDate (D:20261014092211-04'00')
  /ModDate (D:20261024184502-04'00')
>>
endobj

blocks.title: Court E-Filing Risk
blocks.text: Documents filed through court e-filing systems can become part of a public record. Unflattened annotations, live form fields, or leftover metadata in those files may reveal more than you intended. Check your court's own redaction rules and clean files before filing.
5 Places Hidden Data Lives Inside a PDF

items: Document Information Dictionary (/Info): Title, author, creator application, producer, and creation/modification dates.

XMP Metadata Streams (/Metadata): XML packets that can persist even after you edit the basic document properties. They may contain author names, document IDs, and — in files built from photos — camera or location data.

Incremental Save Sections (/Prev pointers): Appended sections at the end of the file that can preserve deleted paragraphs and earlier drafts. See [how to remove PDF revision history](/blog/remove-pdf-incremental-updates-revision-history).
PieceInfo Dictionaries (/PieceInfo): Private working data from design tools such as Illustrator or Photoshop.
Interactive Form Trees (/AcroForm): Field names, default values, and scripts that remain even after a form looks complete.

blocks.text: 3-Step Method to Sanitize a PDF in Your Browser

blocks.title: Load the Document into the Sanitizer
blocks.text: Drop your PDF into the [iKnowAPDF PDF Sanitizer](/tools/sanitize-pdf). The file is read by JavaScript in your browser tab and is not uploaded to a server.

blocks.title: Choose What to Remove
blocks.text: Keep the options to clear the /Info fields and to strip XMP and rebuild the file enabled, and optionally turn on form flattening to bake fillable fields into the page.

blocks.title: Export a Clean Single-Revision PDF
blocks.text: The tool copies the current pages into a new PDF, which leaves behind superseded objects and old revision sections, then downloads the result.
Comparison of Document Sanitization Methods

rows: Yes (pages copied into a new file)

items.question: Does sanitizing a PDF invalidate existing digital signatures?
items.answer: Yes. Certificate-based (PKCS#7) signatures cover the exact bytes of the file. Removing metadata or rewriting the file changes those bytes, so sanitize first and sign last.

items.question: Why process confidential documents in the browser instead of a cloud service?
items.answer: Uploading unredacted documents to a third-party service hands a copy to someone else's servers. Processing locally means the file never leaves your machine, which is easier to square with confidentiality obligations.

items.question: How can I check that metadata was removed?
items.answer: Open the sanitized file in the sanitizer again, or run `pdfinfo sanitized_file.pdf` in a terminal. The author, title, subject, creator and keywords should be empty. Note that new creation/modification dates are written when the file is saved.

items.question: Does sanitizing remove EXIF data inside embedded photos?
items.answer: No. The sanitizer works on document-level metadata. Images embedded in pages are copied as-is, so if a photo's own EXIF data matters, clean the image before putting it into the PDF.

items.question: Does stripping metadata affect searchable text?
items.answer: No. Page content, fonts, and selectable text are copied unchanged. Bookmarks are not carried over when the file is rebuilt.

articles.title: HIPAA and PDF Tools: Why Uploading Patient Records to Cloud Converters Is Risky
articles.seoTitle: HIPAA & Online PDF Tools: Cloud Upload Risks
articles.description: Why uploading patient records to free online PDF converters can create HIPAA problems, and how in-browser processing keeps files on the clinic's own computer.

toolCta.title: Compress Medical PDFs Without Uploading Them
toolCta.description: Compress, merge, split, and clean PDFs in your browser so the file stays on the computer you are using.

blocks.text: Clinical staff, billing specialists, and healthcare administrators often need to merge lab results or shrink large scanned charts for insurance portals and referrals, and a quick web search leads to free online PDF converters. Uploading electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI) to a service that has not signed a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with your organization can be an impermissible disclosure under HIPAA. This article explains the risk and how in-browser tools avoid sending files anywhere.

blocks.title: Not Legal Advice
blocks.text: This article is general information, not legal or compliance advice. Your organization's privacy officer and policies decide which tools staff may use with patient data.
The Business Associate Agreement (BAA) Question

Under HIPAA (45 CFR § 164.502(e) and related provisions), a vendor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of a covered entity is generally a business associate and needs a BAA — even if it says uploaded files are deleted after an hour or two. Many consumer PDF websites do not offer BAAs on free plans. Sending a patient's chart to such a service is the kind of disclosure HIPAA is designed to prevent.
How IT Teams Can Check That a Tool Does Not Upload Files
In-browser tools read the file with JavaScript inside the browser tab. You do not have to take that on trust — you can watch the network activity yourself:

blocks.title: Checking for File Uploads in Browser DevTools
blocks.code:
1. Open https://iknowapdf.lol/tools/compress-pdf
2. Press F12 -> open the "Network" tab
3. Drop a test PDF (not real patient data) and run the tool
4. Look for POST/PUT requests carrying the file: there should be none.
   (Page assets, ads and analytics requests may still appear.)

blocks.title: Why Local Processing Matters
blocks.text: iKnowAPDF's PDF tools process files in your browser, so the documents themselves are not sent to iKnowAPDF's servers. The website still loads normally (and may show ads and use analytics on the free plan), so follow your organization's policy on which websites staff may use.
How Local Processing Relates to HIPAA Technical Safeguards (§ 164.312)

items: Access Control (§ 164.312(a)(1)): The file stays on the workstation of the signed-in staff member instead of a third-party server.
Audit Controls (§ 164.312(b)): Your existing endpoint monitoring still sees the file being opened and saved locally.
Integrity (§ 164.312(c)(1)): Merging and splitting copy pages without re-encoding them. Compression presets that rasterize pages reduce image quality, so check small print before sending.
Transmission Security (§ 164.312(e)(1)): The document is not transmitted while it is being processed. How you send the finished file (email, portal) still needs to follow your usual safeguards.

blocks.text: A Simple 3-Step Workflow for Patient Records

blocks.title: Combine Records Locally
blocks.text: Use [Merge PDF](/tools/merge-pdf) to combine discharge summaries, reports, and consent forms into one packet in the order you choose.

blocks.title: Clean Workstation Metadata
blocks.text: Run [Sanitize PDF](/tools/sanitize-pdf) to clear author names and other document-level metadata before the file leaves your organization.

blocks.title: Compress for Payer & Referral Portals
blocks.text: Use [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf) — or a size-targeted preset such as [compress PDF under 2MB](/compress-pdf-under-2mb) — to get large scanned packets under portal upload caps, then check that small values are still legible.

items.question: Do we need a Business Associate Agreement to use iKnowAPDF?
items.answer: iKnowAPDF does not receive the documents you process — they are handled in your browser — and we do not sign BAAs. Whether a tool that never receives PHI is acceptable is a decision for your privacy officer.

items.question: Can staff use iKnowAPDF without an internet connection?
items.answer: Partly. A service worker caches pages and scripts you have already loaded, so a previously opened tool may keep working offline, but this is not guaranteed for every tool or browser. Don't rely on it for air-gapped networks.

items.question: What happens to the file after the browser tab is closed?
items.answer: The file is held in the tab's memory while you work. Closing or refreshing the tab releases it. The downloaded result is saved wherever your browser saves downloads.

items.question: Does compressing a medical PDF make small lab values harder to read?
items.answer: It can. The Recommended and Extreme presets re-render each page as a JPEG image, which lowers sharpness and makes text non-selectable. For text-heavy reports, try Lossless / High Quality first and always check the output before sending.

articles.title: How to Remove Hidden Revision History and Incremental Updates from PDFs
articles.seoTitle: Remove PDF Revision History & Incremental Updates
articles.description: How PDF incremental saves can leave earlier drafts and deleted text inside the file, and how rewriting the file into a single revision removes them.

toolCta.title: Remove Old Revisions from Your PDF
toolCta.description: Copy the current pages into a fresh single-revision PDF and leave superseded objects behind — in your browser.

blocks.text: When you delete a paragraph, change a pricing table, or crop part of a page in many PDF editors and press 'Save', the old data is not always erased. It can remain inside the file. This is caused by a feature of the PDF specification (ISO 32000-1) called incremental updates. Here is how incremental saves can expose earlier drafts and how to remove them.
How Incremental Saving Leaves Old Versions in the File (ISO 32000 § 7.5.6)

Rewriting a large PDF from scratch used to be slow, so the format allows incremental updates: instead of overwriting changed objects, the editor appends the new versions to the end of the file, writes an extra cross-reference (/XRef) section, and links it to the previous one with a /Prev byte offset. The old objects are still in the file — they are just no longer referenced by the newest section.
How to Spot Incremental Saves Using %%EOF Markers

Each incremental save usually adds another `%%EOF` marker. A file with three `%%EOF` markers may contain three versions, and an earlier version can often be recovered by truncating the file at an earlier marker:

blocks.title: Structure of an Incrementally Saved PDF
blocks.code:
%PDF-1.7
1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >> endobj
... [Original Draft Objects: "$500,000 Acquisition Offer"] ...
xref
0 15
trailer << /Size 15 /Root 1 0 R >>
startxref
18420
%%EOF
... [Appended Revision 2 Objects: "$420,000 Revised Offer"] ...
xref
0 1
4 1
0000024110 00000 n
trailer << /Size 15 /Root 1 0 R /Prev 18420 >>
startxref
29850
%%EOF

blocks.title: Contract Negotiation Risk
blocks.text: If you draft a proposal, delete internal pricing notes, and save incrementally before emailing the PDF, the recipient may be able to recover the deleted revision with freely available tools.
How Rewriting the File Removes Past Revisions

blocks.title: Read Only the Current Pages
blocks.text: Open your PDF in the [iKnowAPDF PDF Sanitizer](/tools/sanitize-pdf). The current page tree is read; superseded object versions are ignored.

blocks.title: Copy the Pages into a New PDF
blocks.text: With 'strip XMP and rebuild' enabled, the current pages are copied into a brand-new PDF document in memory, leaving orphaned objects and /Prev sections behind.

blocks.title: Save a Single-Revision File
blocks.text: The new file is written from scratch with one cross-reference section and one %%EOF marker, so earlier revisions are not carried over.

items.question: Does 'Save As' in a desktop PDF viewer always remove incremental updates?
items.answer: Not always. Some desktop suites fully rewrite the file on 'Save As', but other apps append another update. Copying pages into a fresh document is a reliable way to get a single-revision file.

items.question: Can deleted text be recovered after the file is rewritten?
items.answer: Not from old revisions — unreferenced objects and earlier sections are not copied into the new file. Text that is still on the current page (for example, under a black box) is of course still there; that needs [true redaction](/blog/permanent-pdf-redaction-vector-graphics).

items.question: Why do cropped PDF pages sometimes still contain the cropped-out content?
items.answer: Cropping usually only changes the visible /CropBox while the full page content stays in the file. To remove content, edit or white it out in the [PDF Editor](/tools/edit-pdf), which flattens the edited page into an image on export.

items.question: Does rewriting the file change its size?
items.answer: Usually it gets smaller, because unused objects and old revisions are dropped. If you mainly want a smaller file, use [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf).

articles.title: True PDF Redaction: How to Permanently Remove Text Behind Black Boxes
articles.seoTitle: Permanently Redact PDF Text: Real Redaction vs Boxes
articles.description: The difference between drawing a box over text and actually removing it from the PDF, plus a quick test to check whether a redaction worked.

toolCta.title: Edit, White Out & Flatten PDF Pages
toolCta.description: Delete text in place or cover areas with whiteout. Edited pages are exported as flattened images without the original text.

blocks.text: Botched redaction is a common cause of accidental data leaks in law firms, public records offices, and financial institutions. When redaction is done with ordinary shape or highlight tools, anyone who receives the PDF can select the text under the black box, copy it, and paste the hidden names, numbers, or balances into a text editor.
Why Black Rectangles Fail: Page Content vs. Annotations

A PDF page keeps its main text in the /Contents stream and user markup in a separate /Annots array. Drawing a black box in a basic viewer usually adds a rectangle annotation on top of the text. The text-showing operators (`Tj` and `TJ`) underneath are untouched.

blocks.title: Why the Text Survives Under an Annotation Box
blocks.code:
% Page content stream (/Contents) - STILL SELECTABLE
BT
  /F1 11 Tf
  72 710 Td
  (Confidential SSN: 999-00-1234) Tj
ET

% Black rectangle annotation (/Annots) - only drawn on top
<< /Type /Annot /Subtype /Square /Rect [70 705 240 725] /IC [0 0 0] >>

blocks.title: The 5-Second Copy Test
blocks.text: Before sending a redacted PDF, open the final file, press Ctrl+A (or Cmd+A), copy, and paste into a plain text editor. If the redacted words appear, the redaction failed.
How the iKnowAPDF Editor Removes the Underlying Text

When you edit a line of text or place a whiteout box in the [iKnowAPDF PDF Editor](/tools/edit-pdf), the edited page is re-drawn on a canvas at 2.5x scale with the original text hidden, and that page is replaced by a flattened image when you export. The exported page therefore contains no text operators for the words you removed. The trade-off: text on that page is no longer selectable or searchable.

blocks.title: Open the Document in the PDF Editor
blocks.text: Load your PDF into the [PDF Editor](/tools/edit-pdf). Text lines on the page become editable.

blocks.title: Delete the Text or Apply Whiteout
blocks.text: Click the sensitive line and delete it (or overwrite it with '[REDACTED]'), or use the Whiteout tool to cover any region.

blocks.title: Apply Changes, Then Clean Metadata
blocks.text: Export the PDF, then run it through the [PDF Sanitizer](/tools/sanitize-pdf) to clear document-level metadata such as the title and author, and repeat the copy test.

items.question: Can someone copy text that I deleted in the iKnowAPDF Editor?
items.answer: Not from the edited page: after you apply changes, that page is exported as a flattened image without the old text stream. Always run the copy test on the final file to confirm.

items.question: What if my PDF has 50 pages and I only redact page 3?
items.answer: Untouched pages are copied as normal vector pages; only the pages you edited are flattened into images.

items.question: Should I also sanitize metadata after redacting?
items.answer: Yes. The document title, author, or XMP metadata may still contain sensitive names. Running the [PDF Sanitizer](/tools/sanitize-pdf) clears those document-level fields.

items.question: Is my unredacted file uploaded to a server?
items.answer: No. The PDF Editor and PDF Sanitizer process files in your browser.

articles.title: The Complete Guide to PDF Compression: Lossless vs. Lossy Browser Optimization
articles.seoTitle: PDF Compression Explained: Lossless vs Lossy
articles.description: What makes PDFs large, how lossless object-stream packing differs from page rasterization, and which iKnowAPDF compression preset fits which document.

toolCta.title: Compress a PDF with a Live Size Comparison
toolCta.description: Choose Recommended, Extreme, or Lossless / High Quality and compare before-and-after sizes. Processing happens on your device.

blocks.text: Whether you are emailing a report, uploading a portfolio, or archiving scanned invoices, PDF file size matters. Most people treat compression as a black box — upload, hope, download. Understanding what actually takes up space in a PDF, and what each compression method does to it, lets you pick the right trade-off between size and quality.
What Actually Makes a PDF File So Large?

A PDF is a container of numbered objects: fonts, vector paths, metadata packets, and embedded images (/Subtype /Image). When a 5-page PDF weighs 25 MB, the size usually comes from one of these sources:

items: High-resolution scans and phone photos: Scanners and phone cameras often embed 300–600 DPI full-color images, far more detail than is needed to read a page on screen.
Uncompressed object structure: Older PDF generators write every object header as plain text instead of packing them into compressed object streams (/Type /ObjStm, PDF 1.5+).
Application metadata and thumbnails: Design tools can embed private editing data and preview images.
Duplicate fonts: Merging several PDFs can leave multiple copies of the same font embedded.
Incremental-save leftovers: Repeated edits can append new object versions without removing old ones (see [removing PDF revision history](/blog/remove-pdf-incremental-updates-revision-history)).

blocks.text: Lossless Object-Stream Packing vs. Page Rasterization
The iKnowAPDF compressor (`compressPDFDocument` in our source) offers three presets. It is worth knowing exactly what each one does, because two of them change how your pages are stored:
What Each Preset Does

blocks.title: iKnowAPDF Compression Presets
blocks.code:
1. Lossless / High Quality ("low"):
   - Clears document-level metadata (title, author, producer...)
   - Re-saves with compressed object streams (useObjectStreams: true)
   - Keeps original text, vectors and image bytes untouched
   - Returns the original file if this doesn't make it smaller

2. Recommended ("recommended"):
   - Renders every page to an image at 1.4x scale (about 100 DPI)
   - Encodes each page as a JPEG at quality 0.74
   - Text becomes part of the image (no longer selectable)

3. Extreme & size targets ("extreme" / targetKb):
   - Renders pages at 1.0x scale (about 72 DPI), JPEG quality 0.5
   - With a KB target: picks scale/quality from the per-page budget,
     and runs a second, tighter pass if the first result is too big

blocks.title: The Compressor Never Returns a Bigger File
blocks.text: For Recommended and Extreme, the tool compares the original, the losslessly re-saved version, and the rasterized version, and gives you the smallest of the three. If your PDF is already well optimized, you may get the original back.

rows: Text PDFs exported from Word, Google Docs, LaTeX
Pages re-rendered at ~72 DPI or lower

blocks.text: How much smaller a file gets depends entirely on its content. Scans and photo-heavy PDFs often shrink dramatically with Recommended; text-only PDFs that are already compact may barely change with any preset.
How to Compress Your PDF in 3 Steps

blocks.title: Drop Your PDF into the Compressor
blocks.text: Open [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf). Your file is loaded into browser memory, not uploaded.

blocks.title: Choose a Preset
blocks.text: Pick 'Lossless / High Quality' for text documents you want to keep searchable, 'Recommended' for scans, or 'Extreme' for strict upload limits.

blocks.title: Compare & Download
blocks.text: Review the before-and-after size, open the result to check legibility, and download it.

items.question: What happens if a PDF is already well compressed?
items.answer: The compressor compares the original with each compressed candidate and returns the smallest, so the file will not get bigger. In that case you may simply get the original back.

items.question: When should I choose Lossless over Recommended?
items.answer: If your PDF was exported from Word, Google Docs, or LaTeX and is mostly text, choose 'Lossless / High Quality'. It keeps text selectable and sharp. Recommended turns each page into an image, which suits scans better than text documents.

items.question: Can I target a specific limit like 100KB or 200KB?
items.answer: Yes. Use the size-targeted pages such as [compress PDF under 100KB](/compress-pdf-under-100kb) or [under 200KB](/compress-pdf-under-200kb). They size each page to the budget and run a second, tighter pass if needed. Very long documents may still not fit a small target — splitting them helps.

items.question: Are my PDFs uploaded to a server during compression?
items.answer: No. Rendering and re-saving happen inside your browser on your device.

articles.title: How to Reduce PDF File Size Below 200KB for Strict Portal Uploads
articles.seoTitle: Reduce PDF Size Below 200KB for Upload Portals
articles.description: Practical steps to get scanned IDs, transcripts and forms under 200KB or 100KB for visa, university and job portals while keeping them readable.

toolCta.title: Compress a PDF Under 200KB
toolCta.description: Open the under-200KB preset, which sizes each page to the budget and runs a second pass if needed — in your browser.

blocks.text: Immigration forms, civil service applications, university transcripts, and KYC checks often mean dealing with upload portals that cap each file at 100KB or 200KB. If your scanned passport or certificate is 204KB, the upload simply fails. This guide shows how to get under those limits without making the document unreadable.
Why Do Some Portals Enforce 100KB–200KB Limits?

Portals rarely explain their limits. Small caps keep storage and bandwidth costs down for systems that receive very large numbers of applications, and some older systems were simply built with small limits that were never revised. Whatever the reason, reviewers still need to read fine print, stamps, and the machine-readable zone on a passport, so the goal is the smallest file that stays legible.

blocks.title: Be Careful Where You Upload Identity Documents
blocks.text: Passports, birth certificates, driver's licenses and tax forms are valuable to identity thieves. Prefer tools that process the file on your own device rather than uploading it to an unknown website.
How the iKnowAPDF Size-Target Presets Work

When you use [compress PDF under 200KB](/compress-pdf-under-200kb) or [compress PDF under 100KB](/compress-pdf-under-100kb), the compressor divides the target budget by the number of pages, picks a rendering scale and JPEG quality for that per-page budget, and, if the first pass is still too big, runs one tighter pass:

blocks.title: Size-Target Logic (simplified from src/lib/pdf/pdf-utils.ts)

blocks.text: The scale and quality have lower bounds so pages don't become unreadable, which means a long document may still end up above the target. When that happens, split it into parts.
3 Steps to Get a PDF Under 200KB

blocks.title: Open the Under-200KB Compressor
blocks.text: Go to [compress PDF under 200KB](/compress-pdf-under-200kb); the 200KB target is already set. For other limits there are presets such as [under 100KB](/compress-pdf-under-100kb), [under 300KB](/compress-pdf-under-300kb) and [under 500KB](/compress-pdf-under-500kb).

blocks.title: Drop Your Scanned ID, Transcript, or Form
blocks.text: Run the compressor and check the result size and legibility before uploading.

blocks.title: Split Long Documents if Needed
blocks.text: If a 25-page scan won't fit, use [Split PDF](/tools/split-pdf) to divide it into parts and compress each part separately, if the portal allows multiple files.

items.question: Will passport details and stamps still be readable under 200KB?
items.answer: For 1–4 page documents there is usually enough budget per page to keep text and stamps readable, but results depend on the scan. Always open the compressed file and zoom in on small print before you submit.

items.question: What if my portal requires under 100KB?
items.answer: Use [compress PDF under 100KB](/compress-pdf-under-100kb), or even [under 50KB](/compress-pdf-under-50kb) for very strict forms. Fewer pages make small targets much easier to hit.

items.question: Why is my phone photo of a document so large?
items.answer: Phone cameras capture 12MP or more in full color. Scanning the page with the [document scanner](/tools/scan) and its 'B&W Clean' filter usually produces a cleaner image that compresses much smaller. If you start from a JPG, [JPG to PDF under 200KB](/jpg-to-pdf-under-200kb) handles conversion and size in one step.

items.question: Is there a daily limit on how many files I can compress?
items.answer: No. Compression runs on your own device, and there is no daily cap on how many files you can process.

articles.title: Linearized PDFs & Object Streams Explained: Optimizing Large PDFs for the Web
articles.seoTitle: Linearized PDFs, Object Streams & Fast Web View
articles.description: How PDF object streams, Fast Web View (linearization) and HTTP byte-range requests affect how quickly large PDFs open in the browser.

toolCta.title: Shrink PDFs Before Putting Them Online
toolCta.description: Pack object streams, clear metadata, and reduce the download size of PDFs you host — in your browser.

blocks.text: Have you ever clicked a link to a 60MB catalog or annual report and waited for the first page to appear? Slow PDF loading in the browser usually comes down to two things: the total download size, and whether the file and server allow the viewer to fetch just the parts it needs. This guide explains object streams, Fast Web View (linearization), and HTTP 206 byte-range requests.
Why Traditional PDFs Load Slowly Over HTTP

In a classic PDF, the cross-reference table that tells a reader where each object lives is at the end of the file, just before `%%EOF`. Unless the file is linearized and the server supports range requests, a browser viewer may need to download most or all of the file before showing page 1.
Object Streams (/ObjStm) vs. Annex F Linearization

Two different techniques help here. **Object streams** (PDF 1.5+) pack many small objects into compressed streams, shrinking the file's structural overhead. **Linearization** (ISO 32000 Annex F, often called Fast Web View) reorders the file so page 1 and a hint table come first, letting a viewer show the first page early when the server supports **HTTP 206 Partial Content**:

blocks.title: Example NGINX Config for Serving PDFs
iKnowAPDF Does Not Linearize Files
blocks.text: Our compressor writes object streams and reduces size, but it does not produce linearized (Fast Web View) output. If you need true linearization, use a desktop tool such as qpdf (`qpdf --linearize in.pdf out.pdf`) after compressing.
3 Steps to Make Large PDFs Open Faster Online

blocks.title: Reduce the Download Size
blocks.text: Run the file through [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf). 'Lossless / High Quality' re-packs object streams and keeps text selectable; 'Recommended' shrinks scan-heavy files much more by converting pages to images.

blocks.title: Split Very Large Manuals into Chapters
blocks.text: If you host a 200MB manual, use [Split PDF](/tools/split-pdf) to create chapter-level files so mobile readers download only what they need.

blocks.title: Serve with Byte-Range Support
blocks.text: Host the file on a server or CDN that sends `Accept-Ranges: bytes` and a correct Content-Length, and linearize it with a desktop tool if first-page speed matters.

items.question: What does `useObjectStreams: true` do?
items.answer: Instead of writing every object as a separate plain-text block (`12 0 obj ... endobj`), it packs objects into compressed /ObjStm streams and writes a compact cross-reference stream.

items.question: Why does total file size matter even with byte-range requests?
items.answer: Many mobile browsers and in-app webviews download the whole PDF before rendering it. A smaller file opens faster everywhere.

items.question: Will compressing change how my PDF prints?
items.answer: 'Lossless / High Quality' keeps text and vectors unchanged, so print quality is unaffected. 'Recommended' and 'Extreme' turn pages into lower-resolution images, which is fine on screen but can look soft when printed.

items.question: Is there a file size limit?
items.answer: We don't impose one, but everything runs in your browser's memory, so very large files can be slow or fail on devices with little RAM.

articles.title: How to Fix Bloated Architectural and CAD Vector PDFs That Lag Your Viewer
articles.description: Why PDFs exported from AutoCAD or Revit can freeze tablets and viewers, and when flattening drawings into images is a sensible fix.

toolCta.title: Flatten Heavy CAD Drawings for Field Viewing
toolCta.description: Re-render dense vector sheets as images so they pan and zoom faster on tablets — or keep vectors with the lossless preset.

blocks.text: Architects, engineers, and site supervisors know the problem: you open a 35MB plan set exported from AutoCAD, Revit, or Civil 3D on a tablet, zoom into a detail, and the screen stalls while the viewer redraws. Running the file through a lossless compressor barely changes it. Here is why CAD PDFs lag and what you can do about it.
The Root Cause: Huge Numbers of Vector Paths

When CAD software exports a detailed plan — hatch patterns, contours, insulation symbols, and SHX text exploded into strokes — it can write enormous numbers of individual path operators (`m` moveto, `l` lineto, `c` curveto, `S` stroke) into the page. Every pan or zoom forces the viewer to redraw all of them.

blocks.title: Why Exploded CAD Hatching Is Slow to Render
blocks.code:
% A dense hatch can turn into a very long run of tiny strokes:
0.12 w
412.40 288.15 m 412.55 288.30 l S
412.80 288.10 m 412.92 288.25 l S
... [repeated many thousands of times on one sheet] ...

blocks.title: Why Flattening Helps on Tablets
blocks.text: Re-rendering a dense vector sheet as a single page image (the 'Recommended' preset) means the viewer draws one bitmap instead of re-processing every path, which typically makes panning and zooming much smoother. The trade-off is that you lose vector precision and selectable text.
Choosing Between Lossless Packing and Flattened Field Sets

items: For field review on tablets (use 'Recommended'): Flattens each sheet into an image that scrolls easily. Check that small dimensions are still readable at about 100 DPI.
For vector submittals (use 'Lossless / High Quality'): Clears metadata and re-packs the file while keeping every vector line for measurement on desktop.
For sending only a few sheets (use [Split PDF](/tools/split-pdf)): Extract the 5 relevant sheets instead of emailing the full 120-sheet set.

blocks.title: Load Your Drawing Set into the Compressor
blocks.text: Drop your architectural or engineering PDF into [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf).

blocks.title: Pick 'Recommended' for Speed or 'Lossless' for Vectors
blocks.text: 'Recommended' flattens heavy sheets into images; 'Lossless / High Quality' keeps the vector paths.

blocks.title: Check & Distribute
blocks.text: Open the result on the target device, zoom into fine details, and share it with the field team.

items.question: Does iKnowAPDF keep large sheet sizes like Arch D (24x36) and Arch E (36x48)?
items.answer: Yes. The compressor reads each page's width and height in PDF points and creates the output page at the same size.

items.question: Why did AutoCAD create so many comments in my PDF?
items.answer: Depending on settings, AutoCAD can export SHX text as comment annotations so it remains searchable. The `PDFSHX` system variable controls this behaviour — check your AutoCAD version's documentation before changing it.

items.question: Can I rotate sideways sheets before sending them?
items.answer: Yes. Use [Rotate PDF](/tools/rotate-pdf) to rotate individual sheets by 90° or 180°.

items.question: Are confidential drawings uploaded anywhere?
items.answer: No. Drawings are processed in your browser on your own device.

articles.title: Digital vs. Electronic Signatures in PDFs: ESIGN, eIDAS, and SHA-256 Hashes
articles.seoTitle: Digital vs Electronic Signature in PDF: ESIGN & eIDAS
articles.description: The difference between simple electronic signatures, SHA-256 document hashes and certificate-based digital signatures in PDFs, and when each one is used.

toolCta.title: Sign a PDF in Your Browser
toolCta.description: Draw, type, or upload your signature and optionally append a page listing SHA-256 hashes of the document — processed on your device.

blocks.text: In everyday business, 'electronic signature' and 'digital signature' are often used as synonyms. In law and in the PDF format, they describe different things. Knowing which one a document actually needs helps you avoid both under-protecting important agreements and paying for tooling you don't need.

blocks.title: Not Legal Advice
blocks.text: This article explains general concepts. Signature requirements vary by country, industry and document type — check with a lawyer for anything high-stakes.
Three Levels of Electronic Signatures (US ESIGN Act & EU eIDAS)

The US ESIGN Act and UETA give electronic signatures legal effect in most commercial contexts, and the EU's eIDAS Regulation (No 910/2014) defines simple, advanced, and qualified electronic signatures. In practice you will meet three levels:

items: Simple electronic signature (SES): A drawn, typed, or image signature placed on a document. Widely used for everyday agreements such as NDAs, freelance contracts and purchase orders, although some documents (wills, certain real-estate or court documents) have stricter rules.
Signature plus an integrity record: A simple signature combined with evidence about the document — for example SHA-256 hashes and timestamps — that helps show what was signed and when.

Certificate-based digital signature (AdES/QES, PAdES): Uses an X.509 certificate from a certificate authority, often on a smart card or hardware token, and is embedded in the PDF so that any later change is detected by PDF readers. Qualified signatures are required for some regulated transactions in the EU.

blocks.text: How SHA-256 Document Hashing Works in the Browser

In iKnowAPDF's [Sign PDF](/tools/sign-pdf) tool you can place drawn, typed, or uploaded signatures and date stamps, and tick **'Append Tamper-Evident SHA-256 Audit Certificate Page'**. When enabled, your browser's built-in Web Crypto API computes a SHA-256 hash of the original PDF and of the signed content, and the tool adds a summary page listing both:

blocks.title: Computing a SHA-256 Hash with the Web Crypto API
A Hash Page Is Not a Certificate-Based Digital Signature
blocks.text: The summary page records fingerprints of the file at signing time. It is not a cryptographic PDF signature: PDF readers won't flag later edits automatically, and it doesn't identify the signer with a certificate. Keep your own copies of the original and signed files so the hashes can be checked later, and use a certificate-based signing service when a document requires one.

blocks.title: Open Your Document in Sign PDF
blocks.text: Load the PDF in [Sign PDF](/tools/sign-pdf) and create a signature by drawing, typing, or uploading an image.

blocks.title: Add a Date & (Optionally) the SHA-256 Page
blocks.text: Add today's date stamp and, if you want an integrity record, tick 'Append Tamper-Evident SHA-256 Audit Certificate Page'.

blocks.title: Download and Keep Copies
blocks.text: Download the signed PDF and store it together with the original so the listed hashes can be verified if questions come up later.

items.question: Is a contract signed with iKnowAPDF legally binding?
items.answer: Under the ESIGN Act (15 U.S.C. § 7001) and UETA, a signature can't be denied legal effect solely because it is electronic, and eIDAS has a similar rule for simple electronic signatures. Whether a particular contract is enforceable depends on the parties, the jurisdiction and the type of document — iKnowAPDF can't guarantee that.

items.question: Is my document uploaded when I sign it?
items.answer: No. Creating, placing and hashing signatures all happen in your browser tab.

items.question: Can I save my signature for next time?
items.answer: Yes. Saving a signature stores the image in your browser's localStorage on that device, so you can reuse it. Clear your browser data to remove it.

items.question: Can I add a CONFIDENTIAL or APPROVED stamp while signing?
items.answer: Yes. Sign PDF has an optional diagonal watermark field. For more control over opacity and placement, use [Watermark PDF](/tools/watermark-pdf).

articles.title: PDF Encryption Explained: RC4 vs. AES-128 vs. AES-256 & Cleaning Metadata First
articles.seoTitle: PDF Encryption Explained: RC4, AES-128 & AES-256
articles.description: How PDF encryption evolved from 40-bit RC4 to AES-256, why metadata can stay readable in a locked PDF, and why to clean a file before encrypting it.

toolCta.title: Clean Hidden Metadata Before Encrypting
toolCta.description: Clear document metadata and old revisions in your browser, then encrypt the clean file with the tool of your choice.

blocks.text: Before emailing tax returns, estate plans or board papers, many people add a password to the PDF. Two pitfalls are common: uploading the unencrypted file to an unknown 'free password protector' website, and assuming that a password-protected PDF hides everything — when some encryption settings leave the XMP metadata readable.

blocks.title: What iKnowAPDF Does and Doesn't Do
blocks.text: iKnowAPDF does not currently add or remove PDF passwords. Use it to clean the document first, then encrypt with a trusted desktop tool such as Adobe Acrobat, LibreOffice's PDF export, or qpdf.
PDF Encryption Revisions (R2 to R6)
Not all password-protected PDFs are equally strong. The standard security handler has gone through several revisions:
Even with AES-256, the password is the weak point: a short or common password can be guessed regardless of the cipher. Use a long passphrase.
Why Clean Metadata and Old Revisions Before Encrypting

The PDF standard lets an encryptor leave the XMP /Metadata stream unencrypted (controlled by the /EncryptMetadata flag), mainly so desktop search can index it. When that happens, author names, titles and similar details remain readable even though the page content is locked. Incremental saves can also carry earlier drafts inside the file. Cleaning the document first removes both issues.
Example: Readable Metadata in an Encrypted PDF

blocks.title: XMP Metadata Left Unencrypted (/EncryptMetadata false)
blocks.code:
% Metadata stream left in plaintext when /EncryptMetadata is false
14 0 obj
<<
  /Type /Metadata
  /Subtype /XML
  /Length 1240
>>
stream
<?xpacket begin="" id="W5M0MpCehiHzreSzNTczkc9d"?>
<x:xmpmeta xmlns:x="adobe:ns:meta/">
 <rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#">
  <rdf:Description rdf:about="" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">
   <dc:creator><rdf:Seq><rdf:li>Senior Managing Partner (j.doe@mergers-corp.com)</rdf:li></rdf:Seq></dc:creator>
   <dc:title><rdf:Alt><rdf:li xml:lang="x-default">Acquisition_Project_Titan_v4_Draft.docx</rdf:li></rdf:Alt></dc:title>
  </rdf:Description>
 </rdf:RDF>
</x:xmpmeta>
endstream
endobj

blocks.title: Clean First, Encrypt Last
blocks.text: Run the file through the [PDF Sanitizer](/tools/sanitize-pdf) to clear document metadata and rebuild it without old revisions, then apply encryption as the very last step.

blocks.title: Load the PDF into the Sanitizer
blocks.text: Open [Sanitize PDF](/tools/sanitize-pdf) and drop in your file. It is processed in your browser.

blocks.title: Clear Metadata & Rebuild
blocks.text: Keep the options to clear the /Info fields and strip XMP / rebuild the file enabled.

blocks.title: Encrypt the Clean File
blocks.text: Add an AES-256 password with a trusted desktop tool (for example `qpdf --encrypt <user-pw> <owner-pw> 256 -- in.pdf out.pdf`), and share the password through a different channel than the file.

items.question: Why can metadata be visible in an encrypted PDF?
items.answer: The encryption dictionary can set /EncryptMetadata to false, which leaves the XMP metadata stream unencrypted so it can be indexed. Author names and titles in that stream are then readable without the password.

items.question: Can earlier drafts be recovered from a password-protected PDF?
items.answer: If the file was saved incrementally before encryption, earlier revisions may still be inside it and readable to anyone with the password. Rebuilding the file with the sanitizer before encrypting removes them.

items.question: Does sanitizing reduce image or font quality?
items.answer: No. Pages, fonts and images are copied without re-compression. Only document-level metadata and old revisions are dropped (bookmarks are not carried over).

items.question: Can iKnowAPDF recover a forgotten PDF password?
items.answer: No. iKnowAPDF doesn't crack or remove passwords. Store passwords in a password manager.

articles.title: 'PDF Permissions Restricted' on Bank Statements: What It Means and What You Can Do
articles.seoTitle: Restricted Bank Statement PDF: What You Can Do
articles.description: Why banks restrict statement PDFs with an owner password, what the permission flags control, and legitimate ways account holders can work with these files.

toolCta.title: Combine Statements into One Packet
toolCta.description: Merge statements and supporting documents in the order you choose — in your browser, without uploading financial records.

blocks.text: Accountants, mortgage processors and small business owners regularly download legitimate bank statements, only to find they can't combine them into a tax or loan packet or copy figures into a spreadsheet. The viewer says 'This document has permissions restrictions.' Here is what that means and how to work with such files legitimately.
Why Banks Restrict Statement PDFs

Some banks apply an 'owner password' to statements. This sets a permissions value (/P) in the PDF's security dictionary that asks viewers to disable actions such as printing, copying text, or changing pages. The file still opens without a password, but the content is encrypted and compliant viewers enforce the restrictions.
Anatomy of the /Encrypt Dictionary

blocks.title: Standard Security Handler /Encrypt Dictionary (ISO 32000-1 § 7.6)
blocks.code:
% Owner-password restrictions on a statement
14 0 obj
<<
  /Filter /Standard
  /V 4
  /R 4
  /P -1028        % Permission bits: which actions viewers should allow
  /Length 128
  /U <4a8f9c2d1b...>
  /O <b7e12f6a9e...>
>>
endobj
% Page content is encrypted even though no password is needed to open it

blocks.title: iKnowAPDF Does Not Decrypt PDFs
blocks.text: Our tools don't remove passwords or decrypt files. Because the page content of a restricted PDF is encrypted, running it through tools like Merge or Sanitize may fail or produce blank pages. Use one of the options below instead.
Legitimate Ways to Work with a Restricted Statement

blocks.title: Ask the Bank for an Unrestricted Copy or a Data Export
blocks.text: Most online banking portals offer CSV, Excel or OFX exports of transactions, which are far better for analysis than copying from a PDF. Some banks also provide unrestricted statement copies on request.

blocks.title: Print to PDF if Printing Is Allowed
blocks.text: If the statement allows printing, your operating system's 'Print to PDF' / 'Save as PDF' produces a new, unrestricted file you can then [merge](/tools/merge-pdf) with other documents.

blocks.title: Use a Desktop Tool on Your Own Machine
blocks.text: Desktop tools such as qpdf (`qpdf --decrypt in.pdf out.pdf`) can remove owner restrictions from files you are authorized to use, without uploading them. Then combine and [compress](/tools/compress-pdf) the result as needed.

blocks.title: Keep Client Financial Data Off Unknown Websites
blocks.text: Accountants in the US are subject to the FTC Safeguards Rule under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act. Uploading client statements to random web tools is hard to square with a written information security program — keep processing on systems you control.

items.question: Is it legal to remove restrictions from my own statements?
items.answer: Generally, working with your own records (or a client's, with authorization) for accounting or tax purposes is routine, but rules and bank terms vary by country. When in doubt, ask the bank for an unrestricted copy or a data export.

items.question: Can iKnowAPDF open a PDF if I don't know the password?
items.answer: No. iKnowAPDF doesn't crack passwords or decrypt files.

items.question: Will printing to PDF change transaction amounts or dates?
items.answer: No, the visible content is the same, though the new file may lose selectable text or links depending on your printer driver.

items.question: How do I combine statements once they're unrestricted?
items.answer: Use [Merge PDF](/tools/merge-pdf) to combine them in order, and [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf) if the packet is too large for the lender's portal.

articles.title: How to Keep a Record of Signed PDF Contracts: Audit Trails Explained
articles.seoTitle: Audit Trails for Signed PDF Contracts Explained
articles.description: What an e-signature audit trail is, what it can and can't prove, and how freelancers and small businesses can keep a simple record of signed PDF contracts.

toolCta.title: Sign a Contract with a SHA-256 Summary Page
toolCta.description: Add your signature and date, and optionally append a page listing SHA-256 hashes of the document — in your browser.

blocks.text: Freelancers and small businesses often wonder whether they need a paid e-signature subscription to send a few client agreements. US law (the ESIGN Act and state UETA laws) doesn't require any particular provider. What matters is being able to show that the parties intended to sign, agreed to do business electronically, and that the record wasn't changed afterwards. This article explains what an audit trail contributes and what a simple self-managed approach can and can't do.

blocks.title: Not Legal Advice
blocks.text: Requirements differ by jurisdiction and document type. For high-value or regulated agreements, a dedicated e-signature service or a lawyer's advice is worth it.
Four Things an E-Signature Record Should Show

items: Intent to sign: Each party deliberately applied a signature.
Consent to do business electronically: The parties agreed to use electronic records (often stated in the contract itself).
Association with the record: The signature belongs to this specific document.
Record integrity and retention: You can show the document wasn't altered after signing and you kept a copy.

blocks.text: What a Paid Service Adds

Services like DocuSign or Adobe Sign send the document to each signer by email, log who opened and signed it from which address and when, and apply a certificate-based digital signature so later changes are detected automatically. That third-party log is the main thing a self-managed approach doesn't have.
What the iKnowAPDF Summary Page Contains

In [Sign PDF](/tools/sign-pdf), the optional SHA-256 page records the file name, page count, number of signatures placed, the signing time (UTC), and two SHA-256 hashes computed in your browser: one of the original file and one of the signed content before the summary page was added. For example:

blocks.title: Example SHA-256 Summary Page
blocks.code:
=== CERTIFICATE OF COMPLETION & CRYPTOGRAPHIC AUDIT TRAIL ===
Document File Name: Master_Services_Agreement_2026.pdf
Original Page Count: 8 Page(s)
Signatures / Stamps Placed: 2 Item(s)

SHA-256 DIGESTS:
Pre-Signing Source PDF SHA-256:
  e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
Post-Signing Payload SHA-256:
  8f434346648f6b96df89dda901c5176b10e6d059612d559c41438b2929e741cf

blocks.text: These hashes let you show which original file was signed, as long as you keep that original. They do not identify who signed, and they are not a certificate-based PDF signature, so PDF readers will not warn about later edits.

blocks.title: Agree on Electronic Signing
blocks.text: Include a short clause in the contract stating that the parties agree to sign electronically.

blocks.title: Sign and Add the Summary Page
blocks.text: Open the agreement in [Sign PDF](/tools/sign-pdf), place your signature and date, and tick 'Append Tamper-Evident SHA-256 Audit Certificate Page'.

blocks.title: Exchange and Keep Records
blocks.text: Send the signed PDF to the other party by email (which gives you a timestamped record of delivery), and keep the original, the signed file and the email thread together.

items.question: Will a court accept a contract signed this way?
items.answer: Electronic signatures are generally admissible, but how much weight a record gets depends on the evidence you can produce — who signed, how the document was exchanged, and whether it was changed. Hashes, emails and retained copies all help; for disputes-prone or high-value deals, use a service that independently logs signer identity.

items.question: Where are my signed contracts stored?
items.answer: Wherever you save them. iKnowAPDF doesn't store your documents; the file is processed in your browser and downloaded to your device, so keeping backups is up to you.

items.question: Does the SHA-256 summary page cost extra?
items.answer: No. It is free and computed in your browser with the Web Crypto API.

items.question: Can someone alter the signed PDF after downloading it?
items.answer: Anyone can edit a PDF file. What the hashes give you is a way to check: if you still have your copies, any alteration of the original or signed content produces a different hash. A certificate-based digital signature is needed if you want PDF readers to detect changes automatically.

articles.title: PDF/A-1b & PDF/A-2b Explained: A Practical Guide to Archival PDFs
articles.seoTitle: PDF/A-1b & PDF/A-2b Explained: Archival PDF Guide
articles.description: What PDF/A (ISO 19005) requires — embedded fonts, color output intents, no encryption or scripts — and how to create and validate a compliant archival file.

toolCta.title: Prepare a PDF for Archiving
toolCta.description: Flatten form fields and clear old revisions and metadata in your browser before converting the file to PDF/A with a dedicated tool.

blocks.text: It is easy to assume any PDF will open fine in 20 years. Ordinary PDFs, however, can depend on fonts that aren't embedded, external links, scripts, or device-dependent colors. PDF/A (ISO 19005) is a restricted version of PDF designed for long-term preservation: everything needed to display the document must be inside the file.
Understanding the PDF/A Parts

items: PDF/A-1 (ISO 19005-1, based on PDF 1.4): The original standard. Level 'b' (basic) requires reliable visual reproduction; level 'a' (accessible) additionally requires tagged structure and Unicode text mapping.
PDF/A-2 (ISO 19005-2, based on PDF 1.7): Allows JPEG 2000 compression, transparency, layers, and embedding other PDF/A files.
PDF/A-3 (ISO 19005-3): Like PDF/A-2 but allows embedding arbitrary files such as XML or CSV — used by e-invoicing formats like ZUGFeRD / Factur-X.

blocks.text: Key Requirements Under ISO 19005

To be valid PDF/A, a file must embed all fonts it uses, include an output intent with an ICC color profile (or use only device-independent colors), carry XMP metadata that declares the PDF/A part and conformance level, and avoid features that can't be preserved — JavaScript, audio/video, external content and encryption are not allowed.
Anatomy of a PDF/A OutputIntent Dictionary

blocks.title: OutputIntent Dictionary for PDF/A-1b
blocks.code:
% Output intent referencing an embedded sRGB ICC profile
12 0 obj
<<
  /Type /OutputIntent
  /S /GTS_PDFA1
  /OutputCondition (sRGB IEC61966-2.1)
  /OutputConditionIdentifier (sRGB IEC61966-2.1)
  /RegistryName (http://www.color.org)
  /Info (sRGB IEC61966-2.1)
  /DestOutputProfile 15 0 R
>>
endobj

blocks.title: Who Requires PDF/A?
blocks.text: Many archives, public administrations and some court e-filing systems require or recommend PDF/A for records that must be kept long-term. Requirements differ, so check the exact part and level (for example PDF/A-1b or PDF/A-2b) your recipient asks for.

blocks.title: About the 'PDF/A' Option in iKnowAPDF's Converter
blocks.text: The converter's archival option currently flattens form fields and re-saves the file; it does not embed fonts or color profiles or write PDF/A identification metadata, so its output should not be treated as validated PDF/A. Use a dedicated tool for real PDF/A output.
How to Create a Valid PDF/A File

blocks.title: Prepare the Document
blocks.text: Flatten any form fields and remove old revisions and metadata with the [PDF Sanitizer](/tools/sanitize-pdf), so only the final content remains.

blocks.title: Export or Convert to PDF/A
blocks.text: If you have the source document, export directly to PDF/A from Microsoft Word (Save as PDF → Options → 'PDF/A compliant') or LibreOffice (Export as PDF → 'Archive (PDF/A)'). For existing PDFs, tools such as Adobe Acrobat Pro or Ghostscript can convert them.

blocks.title: Validate the Result
blocks.text: Check the file with the free, open-source veraPDF validator or Acrobat's Preflight. Only a passing validation report shows the file actually conforms.

items.question: Can an encrypted PDF be PDF/A compliant?
items.answer: No. ISO 19005 doesn't allow encryption, so future readers are never locked out by a password or an obsolete cipher.

items.question: Why does PDF/A-1 not allow transparency?
items.answer: PDF/A-1 is based on PDF 1.4 and prohibits transparency to keep rendering predictable, so transparent objects must be flattened. PDF/A-2 and later allow transparency.

items.question: How do I verify that a file is really PDF/A?
items.answer: Validate it with veraPDF (free and open source) or Acrobat Preflight. A file that merely claims to be PDF/A in its metadata isn't necessarily compliant.

items.question: Does converting to PDF/A change the layout?
items.answer: Normally the visible layout stays the same. Converters may substitute fonts that can't be embedded or flatten transparency, so compare the result with the original.

articles.title: OCR for Scanned PDFs: How Text Recognition Works and How to Keep Documents Private
articles.seoTitle: OCR for Scanned PDFs: How It Works & Privacy Tips
articles.description: How OCR turns scanned pages into searchable text, how invisible text layers work in PDFs, and how to run OCR without exposing sensitive documents.

toolCta.title: Scan Paper Documents to a Clean PDF
toolCta.description: Capture pages with your camera or upload photos, crop and straighten them, and apply a black-and-white filter that makes OCR and compression work better.

blocks.text: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) turns pictures of text — scans, phone photos, faxes — into real, searchable text. It is the backbone of paperless workflows. It also raises a privacy question: many online OCR services require you to upload tax returns, medical bills or bank letters to their servers. This guide explains how OCR works and how to pick an approach that fits how sensitive your documents are.

blocks.title: Does iKnowAPDF Do OCR?
blocks.text: Not currently. iKnowAPDF's [document scanner](/tools/scan) creates clean image-based PDFs, and [PDF to Text](/pdf-to-text) extracts text from PDFs that already contain a text layer. For OCR itself, see the options below.
How OCR Works

An OCR engine such as the open-source Tesseract typically cleans up the image (deskewing and thresholding it to black and white), finds lines and words, then recognizes characters with a trained model. Tesseract has also been compiled to WebAssembly (tesseract.js), so OCR can run entirely inside a browser tab — slower than a native app, but without uploading the file.
How Searchable PDFs Hide Text Behind the Image (Render Mode 3 Tr)

blocks.title: Invisible Text Layer in a Searchable PDF
blocks.code:
% Invisible text placed behind the scanned page image
BT
  /F1 10 Tf
  3 Tr          % 3 Tr = neither fill nor stroke (invisible text)
  1 0 0 1 72 710 Tm
  (INVOICE #94821 - TOTAL AMOUNT DUE: $4,850.00) Tj
ET

blocks.title: Why the Scan Looks Unchanged
blocks.text: A 'searchable PDF' keeps the original page image and adds the recognized text invisibly behind it. You see the real scan, but you can search, select and copy the words.
Private Ways to OCR Sensitive Documents

items: Built into your devices: Recent versions of iOS, macOS (Live Text), Android and Windows (Snipping Tool's text actions) can recognize text in images on-device.
Desktop software: OCRmyPDF (free, uses Tesseract) adds a searchable text layer to existing PDFs on your own computer; Adobe Acrobat and other desktop editors also include OCR.
Cloud OCR: Often the most accurate on difficult scans, but it means uploading the document — read the provider's retention and training policies first.

blocks.text: 3 Steps to Get Better OCR Results

blocks.title: Capture a Clean, Flat Scan
blocks.text: Use the [document scanner](/tools/scan) to crop and straighten the page and apply the 'B&W Clean' filter. High contrast and straight lines matter more to OCR than raw resolution.

blocks.title: Run OCR with a Tool You Trust
blocks.text: Use an on-device option from the list above for sensitive documents.

blocks.title: Extract or Compress the Result
blocks.text: Once the PDF has a text layer, [PDF to Text](/pdf-to-text) or [PDF to Word](/pdf-to-word) can pull the text out, and [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf) with 'Lossless / High Quality' shrinks it while keeping the text layer.

items.question: Is on-device OCR as accurate as cloud OCR?
items.answer: For clean, printed documents, good on-device engines are usually accurate enough for search and copy-paste. Cloud services tend to do better on handwriting, low-quality photos and complex layouts. Always proofread numbers that matter.

items.question: Why can't I select text in my scanned PDF?
items.answer: Because the page is just an image. It needs OCR to add a text layer. Our 'Recommended' and 'Extreme' compression presets also turn pages into images, so use 'Lossless / High Quality' if you need to keep an existing text layer.

items.question: Which languages can OCR handle?
items.answer: It depends on the engine. Tesseract supports more than 100 languages through downloadable language data; built-in OS features support fewer.

items.question: Can I get the recognized text into Word?
items.answer: Yes. Once the PDF has a text layer, convert it with [PDF to Word](/pdf-to-word) or extract plain text with [PDF to Text](/pdf-to-text).

articles.title: Merging PDFs Without Losing Bookmarks or Form Data: What to Know
articles.seoTitle: Merge PDFs Without Losing Bookmarks or Form Data
articles.description: Why bookmarks, links and fillable fields often break when PDFs are merged, and practical steps to combine documents without losing the parts you need.

toolCta.title: Merge PDF Files in Your Browser
toolCta.description: Combine documents in the order you choose without uploading them.

blocks.text: Combining PDFs sounds simple, yet merged files often come out with missing bookmarks, broken internal links, or form fields that behave strangely — for example, two documents that both have a field named 'ApplicantName' end up sharing one value. Here is why that happens and how to avoid it.
Three Things That Make Merging PDFs Hard

items: Bookmarks (outlines): Each file's /Outlines tree points at its own pages. A merger has to copy those trees and re-point every entry at the new page objects — many tools simply drop them.
Form fields: Fields live in a document-wide /AcroForm dictionary keyed by name. When two files use the same field names, merging them without renaming causes clashes.
Internal links and named destinations: Links that jump to other pages must be re-mapped to the merged page order or they break.

blocks.text: What a Re-Pointed Bookmark Looks Like

blocks.title: Bookmark Entry After Merging (ISO 32000-1 § 12.3.3)
blocks.code:
% Bookmark whose destination now points at the merged page object
18 0 obj
<<
  /Title (Chapter 2: Financial Exhibits)
  /Parent 2 0 R
  /Next 19 0 R
  /Dest [ 35 0 R /XYZ 0 792 0 ]
>>
endobj

blocks.title: What iKnowAPDF's Merger Keeps
blocks.text: iKnowAPDF's [Merge PDF](/tools/merge-pdf) copies every page — text, images and page content — in the file order you choose. It does not currently rebuild bookmarks, and fillable fields may not stay interactive after merging. The steps below avoid both problems.
How to Merge Without Losing What Matters

blocks.title: Flatten Filled Forms First
blocks.text: If a document contains filled-in form fields, flatten it with the [PDF Sanitizer](/tools/sanitize-pdf) so the entered values become part of the page and survive the merge.

blocks.title: Merge in the Right Order
blocks.text: Add the files to [Merge PDF](/tools/merge-pdf), arrange them in order, and merge. Use [Split PDF](/tools/split-pdf) first if you only need some pages of a file, or [Rotate PDF](/tools/rotate-pdf) to fix sideways pages.

blocks.title: Add Bookmarks Afterwards if You Need Them
blocks.text: If navigation matters (for court bundles or long reports), add bookmarks to the merged file in a desktop editor, or include a table-of-contents page.

items.question: Why do some merge tools drop bookmarks?
items.answer: Copying outline trees and re-pointing every entry at new page objects takes extra work, so many simple mergers only copy pages.

items.question: Will merging keep digital signatures valid?
items.answer: No. Certificate-based signatures cover the exact bytes of the original file, so any merge invalidates them. Merge first, then sign the final document.

items.question: Can I reorder pages from different documents?
items.answer: The merger orders whole files. To interleave individual pages, split the files into the pieces you need with [Split PDF](/tools/split-pdf) first, then merge the pieces in order.

items.question: Is there a limit on how many PDFs I can merge?
items.answer: There is no fixed limit and no upload, but everything happens in your browser's memory, so very large sets may be slow on low-memory devices. If the result is too big to send, run it through [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf).

articles.title: How to Flatten Interactive PDF Forms into Uneditable, Read-Only Records
articles.seoTitle: Flatten PDF Form Fields into Read-Only Records
articles.description: Why the read-only flag doesn't protect a filled PDF form, and how flattening turns form fields into ordinary page content that is much harder to change.

toolCta.title: Flatten PDF Form Fields Locally
toolCta.description: Bake filled-in form fields into the page content in your browser, and clear document metadata at the same time.

blocks.text: When you send a completed insurance claim, lease application, or tax form as an interactive PDF, the recipient can easily change your entries, clear checkboxes, or edit text. Marking fields 'read-only' doesn't really help, because anyone with a PDF editor can switch that flag off. Flattening is the usual answer.
Why the Read-Only Flag Isn't Protection

In a PDF, form fields are widget annotations (/Widget) layered over the page. Setting a field to read-only just sets bit 1 of its field-flags value (/Ff), which tells viewers not to accept input. Any PDF editor can clear that bit and make the field editable again.
What Flattening Does

items: Draws each field's current appearance (its /AP stream) — the text, checkmark or signature you see — onto the page itself.
Removes the interactive fields, so there is nothing left to type into or toggle.
Keeps text as vector text rather than turning the page into a blurry image.
Makes casual editing much harder. A flattened PDF can still be edited like any other PDF with an editor, so keep your own copy if you may need to prove what you sent.

blocks.text: Before and After Flattening

blocks.title: Interactive Widget vs. Flattened Page Content
blocks.code:
% Before flattening: an interactive widget annotation in /Annots
<<
  /Type /Annot
  /Subtype /Widget
  /FT /Tx
  /T (ApplicantFullName)
  /V (Sarah Jenkins)
  /AP << /N 24 0 R >>  % appearance drawn on top of the page
>>

% After flattening: the widget is gone and its appearance
% is drawn as part of the page content
BT
  /F1 12 Tf
  1 0 0 1 120 650 Tm
  (Sarah Jenkins) Tj
ET

blocks.title: Open the Completed Form in the Sanitizer
blocks.text: Drop your filled PDF into [Sanitize PDF](/tools/sanitize-pdf).

blocks.title: Enable Form Flattening
blocks.text: Turn on the option to flatten interactive form fields (it is switched on automatically when the file contains fields).

blocks.title: Download and Check
blocks.text: Open the result and confirm the fields can no longer be edited and all values look right. Then [merge](/tools/merge-pdf) it with other documents or [sign](/tools/sign-pdf) it if needed.

items.question: Can a flattened PDF be unflattened?
items.answer: Not in the sense of getting the original fields back — the values become ordinary page content. Someone could still edit that content with a PDF editor, as with any PDF.

items.question: Does flattening reduce file size?
items.answer: Sometimes slightly, because field dictionaries are removed. For real size reduction, use [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf).

items.question: Are signatures drawn into form fields kept?
items.answer: Signature images and text that appear in fields are kept as part of the page. Certificate-based digital signatures, however, are invalidated by any change to the file, so flatten before applying one.

items.question: Will form calculations still run after flattening?
items.answer: No. Calculated fields are frozen at the values shown when you flattened the form.
